task.title: Cancel pending one-shot schedules
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/791 by durably withdrawing pending intent before any claim or dispatch boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Persist and reopen exact non-blank caller-owned cancellation reason and explicit cancelled status.
Exclude cancelled schedules from due discovery without changing pending ordering.
Return typed missing, duplicate, and racing terminal errors without rewriting valid history.
Reject malformed and impossible cancellation histories fail closed.

attempts.diagnostic: The integration target failed on missing cancellation value, status, store operation, and typed errors.
attempts.patch: Added reopen, due-exclusion, missing, duplicate, malformed-history, and concurrent-cancellation coverage.

attempts.diagnostic: Silently idempotent cancellation would hide repeated caller intent, while deleting the schedule would erase audit evidence.
attempts.patch: Appended an exact reason-bearing event against the projected revision, retained terminal schedules for inspection, and filtered them from due results.

attempts.summary: Verified concurrency and reviewed maintainability findings.
attempts.diagnostic: Hosted review noted a hard-coded pending revision and repeated decode mapping; the revision was correct under the then-exact two-state contract and the optional helper did not justify scope growth.
attempts.patch: Repeated the racing cancellation test, preserved strict replay, updated ADR and scheduler docs, and completed full verification.

outcome.summary: Pending schedule intent can now be withdrawn once with exact durable evidence, while cancelled intent remains inspectable and cannot re-enter due selection.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-kernel --test schedule_store

lessons: Cancellation should preserve why intent was withdrawn instead of deleting the aggregate.
A terminal-state error is safer than silently treating repeated cancellation as success.
Cancellation prevents future selection but does not imply interruption of work selected elsewhere.
Concurrency tests should assert one persisted winner and authoritative typed loser evidence.
Review found a hard-coded pending revision; it was retained because the exact pending-history contract contained one creation event, with revision derivation required if that contract grows.
Review also proposed a shared MalformedPayload mapping helper; that optional low-value cleanup was deferred rather than broadening the cancellation slice.
